back: An automatic check that data is reasonable and allowed; it does not prove the data is correct.
A check that data has been entered or transferred accurately, by comparing with the original or a second copy.
Range, limit, length, format, presence, existence and check digit.
Normal (valid, typical), extreme or boundary (valid, on the edge) and abnormal (invalid, must be rejected), each with an expected result.
Multiply each digit by its weight, add, find the remainder after dividing by 11; check digit = 11 − remainder (0 if the remainder is 0; X if the result is 10).
Visual check (compare screen with source) and double entry (type twice, program compares).
Even parity: the number of 1s, including the parity bit, is even. Detects an odd number of changed bits. Block parity adds a parity byte to find the changed bit.
Sum of the byte values modulo 256, sent with the data and recalculated by the receiver.
A wrong but possible value, such as 58 instead of 85, passes validation.
